answer: Since the pearl index is rebuilt each epoch, the dawn audit can show exactly which earlier answer a submission matched. That makes paraphrasing a losing strategy, because the island embedding ignores word order and synonym substitution alike, so the operator pays authoring cost per alias and collects nothing. Each answer is embedded and compared against the whole corpus, and anything above 75% similarity to an existing answer is rejected as a duplicate before a juror sees it. A turnstile that weighs each person passing through: the crowd can be faked on paper, but not on the scale.
